challenge.name: The Heatwave Blind Spot
challenge.description: A sudden heatwave has shifted demand for seasonal articles, and the current forecast is missing the mark. #model_monica# wants to automate the evaluation harness to test new weather features rapidly, while #requirements_reuben# wants to keep it manual to ensure every test case is rigorously documented before any model change is considered.

output.content: I accept the manual review step for final model approval. I am giving up the full automation of the evaluation harness to ensure every model change passes compliance checks before touching production. This trade-off is necessary to fix the heatwave blind spot. The cost is speed. I lose the rapid iteration cycle for testing new weather features. In exchange, I get the assurance that the manual gate holds. The gate requires a log entry. The log entry requires a form. The form requires approval. The approval requires a meeting. The meeting requires an agenda. The agenda requires a form. The heatwave, meanwhile, is not filling out any paperwork. It is simply raising the temperature of the seasonal articles until the shelf is empty. The compliance check will be thorough. The garden furniture will be unsold. The process is sound. The weather is indifferent.

verdict.reason: The candidate correctly preserves the core fact: the acceptance of a manual review step in exchange for giving up full automation to ensure compliance. It successfully employs the 'recursive bureaucracy' device by chaining the approval process into an infinite loop (log -> form -> approval -> meeting -> agenda -> form). The incongruous layer of the heatwave causing 'garden furniture' to be unsold while the weather remains indifferent to the paperwork provides a concrete, visual illustration of the cost (stagnation/stock issues) without inventing a false causal mechanism; it dramatizes the 'blind spot' by showing the business consequence of the delay. The tone is sharp and the information remains clear.
